clue.text: 'e is adept and can be avoided

parts.note: a dropped-aitch 'he is', contracted to the two letters E and S
adept means skilled or able

explanation.surface: A cockney speaker praises someone's skill, then oddly adds that they can be dodged.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first three words as a cockney sentence: 'E'S CAPABLE, with the H of 'he' dropped and 'is' contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one is able to escape from is, by plain synonym, avoidable.

clue.text: European (Pole) coming back to run off with someone else

indicators.note: coming back tells us the European-plus-Pole string is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European man from Poland returns home to run away with another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns EPOLE round. The brackets make Pole look like a gloss on European, but both words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly with a lover, usually to marry.

clue.text: Insensible jazz fan needs a shot in the arm

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a shot in the arm is a boost, a tonic

explanation.surface: A jazz lover who has passed out needs an injection to revive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot in the arm' looks like a literal injection; here it is the figurative pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is stuporous and unresponsive, so insensible is a fair synonym.

clue.text: A Frenchman consumes fruit in a his second home in town

indicators.note: consumes means the Frenchman's name swallows the fruit, which ends up inside it

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: A Frenchman snacks on fruit at the little flat he keeps in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in a' before 'his' reads as a stray slip in the printed clue and does no work; the hyphens and accent come from the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small residence kept for occasional use, typically a city flat away from the main house.

clue.text: Boy gets scoundrel's shoes

parts.note: a scoundrel is a rogue; with the possessive it gives ROGUE'S

explanation.surface: A lad helps himself to a villain's footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'scoundrel's' vanishes in the grid, leaving ROGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Brogues are sturdy leather shoes with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Card players and coach get on board

parts.note: in bridge the players are named by compass points; East and North give E and N
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Bridge players and their tutor climb aboard together.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge seats are North, South, East and West, so 'card players' can be any two of N, S, E, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a railway carriage, the rail equivalent of embarking.

clue.text: Unhappy Hungarian leaders becoming ascetic

parts.note: unhappy means sad
the leading letters of the word Hungarian, its opening pair

explanation.surface: Gloomy leaders in Budapest renounce worldly comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' here takes the first two letters of Hungarian, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man who lives an austere, renouncing life, so ascetic is an apt noun sense.

clue.text: Try to get fired

definitions.meaning: an attempt, as in 'have a go'
discharged, as a gun is or a bullet

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to get sacked from their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means an attempt and also discharged from a firearm, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Philanthropist has name put in entrance

indicators.note: put in means the abbreviation for name is placed inside the doorway word

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A benefactor has their name inscribed over a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places N inside DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor who gives money to good causes is a giver of gifts, so the synonym fits.

clue.text: A French woman with a couple of articles to disclose

parts.note: un is French for a, the masculine indefinite article
she is a pronoun standing for a woman
two English articles, the indefinite a and the definite the

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman uses a couple of newspaper pieces to reveal something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' sounds journalistic but means grammatical articles: A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe is to draw out from a cover, so uncovering or revealing matches disclose.

clue.text: Dismissed soldier is bizarre

parts.note: in cricket a batsman dismissed is out
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: A soldier discharged from the army behaves strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismissed' borrows the cricket sense: a batsman given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means unconventional and eccentric, the same as strange or weird.

clue.text: Expenses for excursions catching game

indicators.note: catching means the trips word holds the board game inside it

parts.note: excursions are outings
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Money spent on day trips includes a game along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the Japanese board game played with black and white stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings is the British word for money spent regularly, a direct synonym of expenditure.

clue.text: Old transport on river beyond the walls

parts.note: ex means former
a tram is a form of transport
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A vintage tramcar runs along a river outside the city walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural comes from Latin for outside the walls; it now means outside a university's regular courses.

clue.text: Sovereign in charge is unrestricted

indicators.note: in means the monarch's letter sits within the payment word

parts.note: a fee is a charge
R, for Rex or Regina, abbreviates a king or queen

explanation.surface: A monarch who holds power is answerable to nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign in charge' looks like a ruler in control; 'in' puts R inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without restraint or limits is the core sense of the word, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ladies sped off and caused annoyance

indicators.note: off says the letters of the two words are gone wrong and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some women drove away in a hurry and upset everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'sped off' but is the anagram signal on LADIES SPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or offend them, so the past tense matches caused annoyance.

clue.text: Forest guides keep rook within limits

indicators.note: keep means the limits word holds the chess piece's letter
within says the chess letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: ranges are limits or extents
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Woodland guides keep a crow inside the boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the bird but is the chess piece, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Forest wardens who patrol and guide visitors in woodland are called rangers, an example of the job.

clue.text: Research critical? It's on the up and up

parts.note: res. is a dictionary abbreviation for research
critical means pressing, urgent

explanation.surface: Is research vital? It's certainly booming.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the surface; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent means rising again, reviving, the same as steadily improving.

clue.text: Punch hurts during capture

indicators.note: during means the hurts word comes in the middle of the capture word

parts.note: to net is to capture
ails means hurts, troubles

explanation.surface: A blow lands and hurts while someone is being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow; it is the carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a carpenter's punch for driving nail heads below the surface.

clue.text: Doctor accepts the French exhibition

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of accepts are altered and rearranged

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A physician agrees to put on a French show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, and 'accepts' looks like a containment signal; in fact 'Doctor' is the anagram signal and 'accepts' is its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show or display, a synonym of an exhibition.

clue.text: Ties up and watches over aggressive dog

indicators.note: over means the watching word covers and encloses the dog word

parts.note: watches means sees
a cur is a snappish mongrel

explanation.surface: Someone tethers a nasty dog and keeps an eye on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watches over' looks like one phrase meaning guards; 'over' is the containment signal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To make fast or fasten something, as a rope round a post, is to tie it up.

clue.text: Student's small choral composition

definitions.note: read as 'student is', a learned student

indicators.note: composition signals the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil's brief piece of music for choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student's' is 'student is', the definition plus a link. 'composition' looks musical but rearranges CHORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person or pupil devoted to study is the core sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Excellent drink taken with army engineers

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A fine tipple shared with a unit of army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means highest in quality, so it serves as a synonym of first-rate.

clue.text: Boy has song from old capital of Israel

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A lad sings a melody from the ancient Israelite capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Samaria was the capital of the northern Kingdom of Israel in biblical times.

clue.text: Rex remains impulsive

parts.note: Rex, Latin for king, is abbreviated R
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: The leftovers of a king prove hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thought, hasty and reckless, is the standard adjective sense.

clue.text: Religious teacher grew dizzy on island

parts.note: one's head swam, meaning one grew dizzy

explanation.surface: A guru felt giddy while on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grew dizzy' is the idiom 'my head swam', not swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu holy man and spiritual guide, an example of a religious teacher.

clue.text: Parliament has money for the wine

parts.note: a chamber is a legislative assembly
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Parliament holds funds earmarked for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is dated British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin, an example of a wine.

clue.text: Model wearing cape, retreats

indicators.note: wearing means the headland word goes around the car letter, like clothing

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A fashion model wears a cape and then backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is Ford's Model T; 'wearing' puts T inside NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy hideaways or places of refuge are nests in the figurative sense, plural like retreats.

clue.text: Request to entertain royal composer

indicators.note: to entertain means the plea word hosts the royal letter within

parts.note: to beg is to request
R abbreviates royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A plea for a monarch to be amused by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' puts R inside BEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, an example of a composer.

clue.text: Bank clerk losing head conceals reputation of craftsman

indicators.note: conceals means what remains of the clerk word hides the reputation word inside
losing head means the first letter of the clerk word is dropped

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk
a name is a reputation, as in making a name

explanation.surface: A beheaded bank clerk hides a craftsman's good standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the first letter of the clerk word, leaving ELLER, which then holds the reputation word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who applies a glassy vitreous coating to metal or pottery is an artisan, an example of a craftsman.

clue.text: Belts and hosiery

definitions.meaning: punches or wallops, as in hitting someone hard
short stockings worn on the feet

explanation.surface: Waist straps and stockings on a clothing list.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hits hard and foot garments; the surface pairs two garments to hide the verb.

clue.text: Poor girl's obsession?

parts.note: poor means meagre or thin, as in a poor turnout
G is a dictionary abbreviation for girl; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: What does a girl without money fixate on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' hints at a lack of money but means meagre; the question mark flags that G for girl is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fixation about something is idiomatically called having a this-word about it, as with spiders.

clue.text: Study clothes to change the point of delivery

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
dress means clothes

explanation.surface: A student's outfit has to be sent to a new address.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a letter is to alter where it is sent, so the postal sense matches.
